summary: Service page of Silver Oak Capital (London-based debt advisory / finance broker) for property development finance. The page positions the firm as a source of flexible funding for residential, commercial or mixed-use projects (borrowing, development, refinancing, acquisition). Development finance is described as funding for property developers and property investors building real estate schemes 'of any nature', ground-up or conversions. Mechanics stated on the page: the loan is secured against the available land, drawn down in line with the business plan and construction schedule, interest is not serviced but rolled up on top of the principal, and the loan is repaid at practical completion through sales proceeds or refinance. The page claims '300+ Lenders' and 'access to the largest network of lenders in the market' (seed adds: vast network of senior debt, mezzanine debt and equity lenders; typically 3 or 4 potential partners per deal). Other pages of the same site give different lender counts (800+ on home and in a LinkedIn post, 500+ on the LinkedIn profile) and a minimum deal size of £500,000 (home, /lenders/) versus 'over £2m' on an older cached page. No page headings, FAQ block, calls to action, rates, LTV/LTGDV figures, fees or timescales from this specific page were surfaced by the searches; the LTGDV ranges (65-70%, 65-75%) and durations (18-24 months) recorded below come from sibling pages (/conversions/, /faq/, Scotland guide).
